alg-ilu0-fixed-pattern-factorization:
## Definition

Let $F$ be a field, let $n\ge1$, and let the input be a valid $n\times n$ CSR
record as in [[def-csr-matrix-with-stored-entry-semantics]], representing
$A\in M_n(F)$. Matrix positions in this definition use one-based notation:
$(i,j)$ refers to CSR row $i-1$ and column index $j-1$. This row/column order
is fixed before the procedure begins; the procedure performs no pivoting or
reordering. All field operations below are exact.

Let $P=\{(i,j):a_{ij}\ne0\}$. Scan each row once to check the canonical and
increasing-index conditions and to record whether its diagonal position occurs.
If the input fails either pattern condition, return `invalid-pattern`. If a row
has no diagonal position, return `missing-diagonal(i)` for the least such $i$.

Copy the value in each input slot to a work array $W$, and regard the unit
diagonal of $L$ as implicit. Process rows $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order.
For each $k<i$ with $(i,k)\in P$, in increasing $k$ order, do the following:

1. If $W_{kk}=0$, return `zero-pivot(k)`.
2. Set $W_{ik}\gets W_{ik}/W_{kk}$; this value is the stored factor $L_{ik}$.
3. Traverse the two increasing lists
   $\{j>k:(i,j)\in P\}$ and $\{j>k:(k,j)\in P\}$ by a two-pointer merge.
   For each matching index $j$, update
   $$W_{ij}\gets W_{ij}-W_{ik}W_{kj}.$$

After all such $k$ have been processed in row $i$, if $W_{ii}=0$, return
`zero-pivot(i)`. Otherwise the upper row entries $U_{ij}$ are the current
$W_{ij}$ for $(i,j)\in P$ and $j\ge i$. Continue to the next row.

If every row completes, return `ok` with the unit-lower factor $L$ (stored
strict-lower entries $L_{ik}=W_{ik}$ for $(i,k)\in P$) and the upper factor
$U$ (stored entries $U_{ij}=W_{ij}$ for $(i,j)\in P$, $j\ge i$). Both factors
use only positions in $P$; the diagonal of $L$ is implicit. The numeric values
remain stored at their structural slots if an update makes a value zero.

For a successful factor pair and $r\in F^n$, apply the preconditioner by
forward substitution
$$y_i=r_i-\sum_{k<i}L_{ik}y_k\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n),$$
followed by backward substitution
$$x_i=\frac{y_i-\sum_{k>i}U_{ik}x_k}{U_{ii}}\qquad(i=n,n-1,\ldots,1).$$
The pivot checks ensure every denominator in this application is nonzero. This
procedure defines setup and application only; it asserts no factorization
identity $A=LU$, Krylov convergence, conditioning improvement, or accuracy
guarantee.
thm-ilu0-factor-pattern-and-work-counts:
## Statement

Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge1$, and $A\in M_n(F)$ have a valid canonical CSR
record with strictly increasing column indices in each row. Let
$P=\{(i,j):a_{ij}\ne0\}$ and $s=\operatorname{nnz}(A)$. Run
[[alg-ilu0-fixed-pattern-factorization]]. The procedure terminates with a
`missing-diagonal` or `zero-pivot` status, or returns `ok`.

On an `ok` return, define
$$P_L=\{(i,k)\in P:i>k\},\qquad P_U=\{(k,j)\in P:k\le j\},$$
and put $\ell=|P_L|$, $q=|P_U|$, and $u=q-n$. The stored strict-lower
slots of $L$ are exactly $P_L$, and the stored slots of $U$ are exactly $P_U$;
the unit diagonal of $L$ is implicit. Thus the factors use exactly
$\ell+q=s$ numeric slots. Here a factor's stored-slot count retains a slot
even if an update makes its value zero.

For each $(i,k)\in P_L$, let
$$R_{ik}=\{j>k:(i,j)\in P\},\qquad C_k=\{j>k:(k,j)\in P\},$$
and set $I=\sum_{(i,k)\in P_L}|R_{ik}\cap C_k|$ and
$J=\sum_{(i,k)\in P_L}(|R_{ik}|+|C_k|)$. On a successful setup, the
factorization performs exactly $\ell$ divisions, $I$ multiplications, and
$I$ subtractions. The two-pointer merges perform at most $J$ column-index
comparisons, in addition to one validation visit for each of the $n$ row
intervals and the $s$ stored entries.

Applying a successful factor pair to one vector by the specified two
triangular solves performs exactly $\ell+u=s-n$ multiplications, $s-n$
subtractions, and $n$ divisions, and returns the unique vector produced by
forward and backward substitution. These counts concern setup and one
application separately. They assert no convergence, conditioning improvement,
or accuracy guarantee. The stored-pattern conclusion is about $L$ and $U$;
it does not assert that the product $LU$ has support contained in $P$.
alg-flexible-gmres-variable-right-precon:
## Definition

Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$ with $n,m\ge1$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), let
$A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ ([[def-matrix-space]]), and let $b,x_0\in\mathbb C^n$.
The complex scalars form a field ([[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]).
Equip $\mathbb C^n$ with the standard Hermitian inner product
$$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k<n}z_k\overline{w_k}$$
and its induced Euclidean norm $\|z\|_2=\sqrt{\langle z,z\rangle}$
([[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]], [[def-inner-product-norm]]).
All arithmetic and orthogonalization are exact. Iteration and auxiliary
Hessenberg labels below start at $1$; coordinates of $A$ and ambient vectors
retain the library's zero-based convention.

At step $j$, a right-preconditioning action
$\mathcal P_j:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^n$ ([[def-function-space]]) supplies
$z_j=\mathcal P_j(v_j)$. The actions may vary with $j$; no linearity or
fixedness is assumed. In the usual matrix case this is
$z_j=M_j^{-1}v_j$ for an invertible $M_j$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]). The algorithm uses and
stores each actual $z_j$ and makes no fixed-matrix assumption.

Set $r_0=b-Ax_0$ and $\beta=\|r_0\|_2$. If $\beta=0$, return
`initial-solution($x_0$)`. Otherwise set $v_1=r_0/\beta$. For
$j=1,\ldots,m$, perform:

1. Obtain $z_j=\mathcal P_j(v_j)$ and set $w:=Az_j$.
2. For $i=1,\ldots,j$ in order, set
   $$h_{ij}:=\langle w,v_i\rangle,\qquad w:=w-h_{ij}v_i.$$
3. Set $h_{j+1,j}:=\|w\|_2$. If $h_{j+1,j}=0$, return
   `breakdown($j,x_{j-1}$)` with the last fully formed iterate (for $j=1$ it
   is $x_0$); do not normalize or claim a new iterate at this step.
4. If $h_{j+1,j}>0$, set $v_{j+1}:=w/h_{j+1,j}$. Let $e_0\in\mathbb C^{j+1}$
   be the standard unit vector at coordinate $0$ (coordinate $0$ is $1$ and
   all other coordinates are $0$; [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]]). Put
   $Z_j=[z_1,\ldots,z_j]$ and let $\bar H_j$ be the $(j+1)$-by-$j$ matrix
   with entries $h_{ik}$ for $1\le i\le k+1$, $1\le k\le j$, and zero
   entries below that range. Choose any
   $$y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb C^j}\|\beta e_0-\bar H_jy\|_2$$
   and set $x_j:=x_0+Z_jy_j$.

If all $m$ steps complete without breakdown, return
`budget-complete($m,x_m,Z_m$)`. The finite-dimensional least-squares minimizer
exists; the output relation permits any minimizer. The algorithm has no
convergence test: `budget-complete` and `breakdown` assert neither convergence
nor that a breakdown iterate solves $Ax=b$. The residual-minimization property
over the actual span of the $z_j$ is proved separately in
[[thm-flexible-gmres-residual-minimization-on-actual-preconditioned-span]].
Every division is by a positive real norm: the initial $\beta=0$ case returns
before normalizing $r_0$, and each later $h_{j+1,j}=0$ case returns before
normalizing $w$.
thm-flexible-gmres-residual-minimization:
## Statement

Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ and $b,x_0\in\mathbb C^n$, with the standard
Hermitian inner product and induced Euclidean norm. Suppose the algorithm
[[alg-flexible-gmres-variable-right-preconditioning]] completes $m\ge1$ steps
without breakdown, producing $Z_m=[z_1,\ldots,z_m]$, the matrix
$V_{m+1}=[v_1,\ldots,v_{m+1}]$, and $\bar H_m$. Then
$$AZ_m=V_{m+1}\bar H_m,$$
and every $y\in\mathbb C^m$ satisfies
$$b-A(x_0+Z_my)=V_{m+1}(\beta e_0-\bar H_my),\qquad \|b-A(x_0+Z_my)\|_2=\|\beta e_0-\bar H_my\|_2.$$
Consequently every least-squares minimizer $y_m$ in the algorithm produces a
true-residual minimizer $x_m=x_0+Z_my_m$ over
$$x_0+\operatorname{span}\{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}.$$
Moreover, $\bar H_m$ has full column rank, so its least-squares minimizer is
unique.
The result makes no fixed-preconditioner spectral or convergence claim.
